For line 179 below:  AI Overview         
This code is written in R using the data.table package. It creates a new column named grank in the data table betw_group, which assigns a rank to rows based on the values in the between column.

Here is a breakdown of the code "betw_group[, grank := rank(-between, ties.method = 'average')]"

Detailed Breakdown
  * betw_group[...]: This indicates an operation on the data.table named betw_group.
  * grank :=: The := operator is used in data.table for in-place assignment. It creates a new column named grank (or updates it if it exists) without making a copy of the entire data frame.
  * rank(...): This is the R function used to calculate ranks.
  * -between: The minus sign indicates that the ranking is done in descending order (highest value gets rank 1).
  * ties.method = 'average': This dictates how to handle ties (cases where between has identical values). The "average" method assigns the mean of the ranks that the tied values would have received. For example, if two values are tied for 2nd and 3rd place, both receive a rank of \(2.5\).

Summary of Result
The grank column will contain numeric values representing the rank of the between column, where the highest value is ranked 1, with average ranks assigned to ties.

Note: For faster, more efficient ranking in data.table (especially with large datasets), frank is often used instead of rank.



```{r e-big) PageRank measure of citation importance}

prank <- page_rank(cit_graph)
V(cit_graph)$prank <- unlist(as.vector(prank$vector))

betw <- betweenness(cit_graph)
V(cit_graph)$betweenness <- as.vector(betw)
betw_group <- data.table(node = V(cit_graph)$name,
                         between = betw,
                         group = V(cit_graph)$louv_cluster)
betw_group[,grank:=rank(-between,ties.method = 'average'),by=.(group)]

# when using "data.table" package, 
# don't have to re-store or re-assign variable
    # so the code above DOES create a column for "grank" even though it doesn't look like it
        # (which is why the next line is able to call it)

V(cit_graph)$high_between <- V(cit_graph)$name %in% betw_group[grank<=4,]$node

# Liza commented out the next line
# V(cit_graph)[betw == max(betw)]

prank_max <- data.table(node = V(cit_graph)$name,
                        group = unlist(V(cit_graph)$louv_cluster),
                        pagerank = unlist(V(cit_graph)$prank))

prank_max_by_group <- prank_max[,max(pagerank),by=.(group)]

max_by_group = dplyr::left_join(prank_max,prank_max_by_group)[pagerank==V1,]

V(cit_graph)$highest_in_group <- V(cit_graph)$name %in% max_by_group$node

saveRDS(cit_graph, "indig_clusters_full.rds")
# indig_cit_full <- readRDS(file = "data/indig_clusters_full.rds")

```
